sourceRegistry.title: Building advertising for the way people use AI
sourceRegistry.factSummary: OpenAI announced visual ads for ChatGPT. Testing is planned to begin later in October 2026 in the United States. Ads will appear during image generation, be clearly labeled, and remain separate from the generated image.

sourceRegistry.title: Our approach to EU text provenance rules
sourceRegistry.factSummary: Invisible watermarks are planned for eligible ChatGPT and Codex text output in the EU over coming weeks. The mark signals OpenAI involvement in producing or processing the text. The mark does not identify the user or establish the truth of the text.

concepts.title: Keep the noun and adjective together.
concepts.explanation: Egyptian adjectives normally follow the noun. A masculine noun takes the masculine form: نص جديد (nass gedeed, a new text). A feminine noun takes the feminine form: صورة جديدة (soora gedeeda, a new picture). Compare خطة جديدة (khetta gedeeda, a new plan). In a simple present description there is no separate word for “is”: الصورة جديدة means “The picture is new”.

concepts.title: Say what you are doing.
concepts.explanation: بقرا (baʾra) means “I read/am reading”, and بشوف (bashoof) means “I see”. أنا (ana, I) is optional because the verb already carries the person. Put the thing read or seen after the verb. Unlike Hungarian, Egyptian Arabic does not add an object ending to these nouns: نص stays نص. Use الـ for a specific “the”: نص is “a text”, النص is “the text”.

concepts.title: Read the future forms
concepts.explanation: The future prefix ha- points forward: هتبدأ (hatibdaʾ) is “will start”; هيظهر (hayezhar) is “will appear”. After ha-, t- agrees with the feminine تجربة (tagriba, test/trial), and y- agrees with the masculine إعلان (eʿlaan). Learn the time phrase الشهر ده (esh-shahr da, this month) as one chunk.

examples.english: while you are making an image

concepts.title: Describe the mark
concepts.explanation: علامة (ʿalaama, mark) is feminine, so “not visible” becomes مش باينة (mesh baayna). Compare النص مش باين (the text is not visible) with العلامة مش باينة (the mark is not visible). عندها (ʿandaha) means “she/it has”; here it refers to the company. The long second line is supported reading: recognise نصوص (texts), علامة (mark), and the EU place name.

concepts.title: Ask what someone is reading
concepts.explanation: بتقرا إيه؟ (betʾra eeh?) asks a man “What are you reading?” إيه (eeh, what) comes after the verb in this natural question. بقرا (baʾra) answers “I read/am reading”. Use ده (da) with the masculine إعلان and دي (di) with the feminine صورة. عنها (ʿanha) means “from it/her” and refers back to the picture. Mona uses شايفة (shaayfa) for what she can see right now; a man would say شايف (shaayef). The chunk بشوف (bashoof) is common for seeing in general or habitually.

examples.english: What are you reading? (to a man)

concepts.title: Read the sounds
concepts.explanation: Transliteration: aa, ee, and oo are long vowels; sh is ش; kh is خ; gh is غ; ʿ is ع; ʾ is the glottal stop. Egyptian ج is usually g. The article is written el-, or with its assimilated sound in forms such as en-nass. Read the script first if you can, then use transliteration as support.

concepts.title: Review tomorrow, then after a gap
concepts.explanation: Tomorrow: recall “The model helps” first. Then recall picture, text, and advertisement without the word list. In three days: pair each with “new” and check its gender. In seven days: rebuild a two-line reading conversation. If a form is unfamiliar, learn it now and revisit it later; no previous completion is assumed.

Review: previously authored vocabulary. Try it from memory if familiar.
Third-person singular present. The subject can come before the verb.

concepts.title: What do you see? Mark the object.
concepts.explanation: The object is the thing you see or read. Hungarian usually marks it with -t. Sometimes a vowel comes before the -t: kép → képet, szöveg → szöveget, hirdetés → hirdetést. Learn these three forms as chunks. Compare A kép új (“The picture is new”) with Látok egy képet (“I see a picture”): the first picture is the subject, the second is the object. Keep egy (“a/an”) in today’s production examples, because a definite object uses a different verb form.

examples.english: I am reading a new text.

concepts.title: Describe something now; place it in the future.
concepts.explanation: For a present-tense statement about what one thing is like, use noun + adjective: A kép új. There is no van between them. But van is used in the learned expression külön van (“is separate”). To speak about the future, külön lesz means “will be separate”. The news also uses fog + infinitive: fog tesztelni, “will test”. Recognise this future pattern today; your own sentences can stay in the present.

concepts.title: Read the future forms
concepts.explanation: Start with the familiar nouns: hirdetés is an ad, kép is a picture. In hirdetések, -ek marks the plural. Fog tesztelni means “will test”: fog + an infinitive in -ni expresses a future action. Ebben a hónapban gives the time, so indul (“starts”) can describe the planned future test. Treat the longer place and time expressions below as reading support.

examples.english: receives clear labeling; will be clearly labeled in this future context

concepts.title: Describe the mark
concepts.explanation: Láthatatlan means “invisible”; nem látható means “not visible”. Both describe the mark. In a simple present description such as A jel láthatatlan, Hungarian has no separate word for “is”. Egyes means “some” here. You do not need to produce the long second sentence: use its English support and recognise ChatGPT, Codex, and Európai Unió.

concepts.title: Ask what someone is reading
concepts.explanation: Mit olvasol? asks “What are you reading?” Compare olvasol (“you read”) with olvasok (“I read”). The ending tells you who is reading, so Bence does not need én (“I”). In A szöveg is rövid, is means “too/also”, not the English verb “is”.

concepts.title: Read the sounds
concepts.explanation: Hungarian stress falls on the first syllable. Accents matter: kép has a long é, and hír has a long í. Read sz as English s (szöveg) and s as English sh (olvasok). Say each chunk slowly, then say its whole example.

concepts.title: Review tomorrow, then after a gap
concepts.explanation: Tomorrow: recall “The model helps” first. Then recall kép, szöveg, and hirdetés with their object forms. In three days: rebuild the three sentences without a word bank. In seven days: describe a different picture and text. If a form is unfamiliar, learn it now and revisit it later; no previous completion is assumed.
